title: Implement quantile-aware throughput stabilizer and sustained-delta rollout guard
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Adds a quantile-aware stabilizer to reduce false-positive throughput regressions during transient load/warmup and a sustained-delta rollout guard that requires multisignal confirmation (p50+p95+throughput) before automatic rollbacks.
description: Motivation: We continue to see noisy throughput regressions from short-lived traffic spikes and pod warmups that trigger canary rollbacks unnecessarily. This PR adds a lightweight Quantile-Aware Throughput Stabilizer (QATS) and a Sustained-Delta Rollout Guard to the perf-canary service. QATS maintains rolling quantile summaries (p10/p50/p95) and applies an adaptive smoothing window that is smaller for median and larger for high-percentiles; the stabilizer computes a statistically robust delta across quantiles and ignores transient spikes shorter than configurable persistence. The rollout guard requires aligned deltas across p50+p95+throughput for a sustained window before recommending automated rollback. Changes: 1) New detector implementation and unit tests 2) Config knobs (persistence, quantile weights, min-sample-size) exposed via canary config and Helm values 3) Integration: the canary decision pipeline now merges QATS signal with existing anomaly detectors, prioritizing stability during cluster churn and autoscaling. Backwards compatibility: default behavior is conservative (stabilizer off by default for existing customers); enabling is opt-in via canary config. Testing: benchmark harness run against historical canary windows (stage/stripe) and synthetic warmup traces; results summarized below. Checklist: - [x] Detector implementation with docs - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Helm values and example config - [x] Benchmarks and staging verification - [x] Review from SRE and Perf teams

benchmarks_summary: Stage harness: ran 50 historical canary windows and 120 synthetic warmup traces. Baseline false-positive rate: 18%. With QATS + sustained-delta guard enabled: false-positive rate: 5% (relative reduction 72%), detection latency for true regressions increased by median 4s (within acceptable SLO). CPU overhead: +3-5% on canary worker; memory overhead: ~150KB per active canary.
